name: aizen-tech-learning
description: Deep, layer-by-layer technology research with architecture diagrams and architecture-based comparison, published to Notion

steps.hint: official docs, the source repo at the version tag, the design paper
the Notion page URL (waive with evidence when Notion is missing)

expectations.text: The thesis names the one or two design choices that win this workload, by component ID, and the price paid
Each relevant layer explains the mechanism with a counted cost (copies, syscalls, round-trips, O(...), locks) and an Observe command
Every claim about the technology's internals links to the source code or docs at the researched version
The core algorithm section states its invariants, complexity and the breaking point workload with the reason
Each alternative runs the same operation through the same layers; the verdict is 'choose X when <condition>'
After reading, someone could say why it is fast in this workload and when it stops being fast
